component.name: Try Omarchy
component.summary: Try the Omarchy desktop in a window

description.p: Try Omarchy runs the Omarchy desktop in a virtual machine, so you can explore its apps, themes and keyboard-first workflow without replacing your current distro or repartitioning a drive.

ul.li: Start with a ready-to-use trial account, or make Omarchy your own
GPU accelerated graphics, with software rendering as a fallback
Clipboard and file sharing with your desktop, plus an optional shared folder
A persistent disk with backup, restore and move
Settings for memory, processors, display scale and microphone access

description.p: The first launch downloads Omarchy, about 2 GB, and needs about 13 GB of free space for Omarchy, plus space for the Flatpak runtime. The app needs a 64-bit x86 PC with hardware virtualization and access to KVM. Removing the app keeps your VM unless you also delete its data.

Set up Omarchy from the Try Omarchy launcher

description.p: First release of Try Omarchy for Linux.

ul.li: The launcher now matches Try Omarchy for Mac and Windows, with Settings grouped into General, Devices and Advanced pages
Local port forwards change when you save Settings while Omarchy runs
Backups keep the window responsive, and a slow first account setup no longer shows as a failure
Stopping Omarchy while it starts shuts it down cleanly
The home screen shows the shared folder's name
Switch playback and microphone devices while Omarchy runs
Use a camera through your desktop's permission portal
Release the keyboard when the pointer leaves the window on Wayland
Keep unsupported clipboard sharing out of startup error windows
Setup asks how you want to sign in before it downloads Omarchy, with your own account as the default and a quick-start account as the alternative
SSH accepts only keys for the quick-start account, since its password is public
On X11 desktops, Omarchy releases the keyboard when the pointer leaves its window
The clipboard helper stops when Try Omarchy closes
Updates now come from flatpak.tryomarchy.com, and existing installs switch to it automatically
Software shows screenshots and a short video of the app
Updates now come through Software from the Try Omarchy repository
The home screen shows what setup needs, where your VM lives and how much space it uses
Setup says whether it is downloading, preparing or starting Omarchy, resumes interrupted downloads and can try again in place
A short explanation comes before GNOME's clipboard permission, and Settings can turn sharing on or off
Ctrl+Alt+G gives the keyboard back to your desktop, and a one-time tip says so
Backup and recovery can remove what an interrupted backup or restore left behind
Settings groups its options under clear headings

description.p: First preview of Try Omarchy for Linux.
